### Catatonia
A psychiatric state described in the transcript as being "pulled into their shell," in which the person is very aware of everything going on around them but is unable to reach outside themselves and relate to others. The speaker notes this is an accurate clinical description, as individuals can later report what they were observing and thinking during the episode.

### Psychiatric Hospitalization
Inpatient admission to a psychiatric hospital, referenced in the transcript in the context of the client's two admissions in 1975 and 1976. The first lasted two to three months and was associated with catatonic presentation and one delusion; the second ended when the client chose to leave on his own by walking away and returning home.

### Grounds Privileges
A status within an inpatient psychiatric setting that permits a patient to move freely on the hospital grounds. In the transcript, the client used this privilege to walk away from the hospital and return home during his second hospitalization.

### Delusion
Mentioned briefly in the transcript as one symptom present at the time of the client's first psychiatric hospitalization, specifically described as involving one person. No further clinical elaboration is provided by the speaker.

### Nubbin of Self
A phrase used by the presenter to describe a small but meaningful expression of individual autonomy or self-definition. It is applied in two instances: the client walking away from the psychiatric hospital on his own volition, and the client's firm refusal to pay his daughter's rent, both interpreted as signs of a preserved sense of self.

### OCD (Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder)
Referenced in the transcript as a concern the client's daughter raised about herself within the last couple of years. The client responded by gathering and providing her with relevant information, after which the symptoms appeared to settle down. No clinical definition is offered by the speaker beyond this usage.

### Joint Custody
A post-divorce parenting arrangement described in the transcript in which both parents share involvement in the child's upbringing. In this case, the client had the daughter on weekends initially and later on weeknights as well, and is described as having been consistently active in her life rather than an absentee father.

### Neuropathy
A physical health complication experienced by the client, listed alongside a paralyzed vocal cord and difficulty swallowing as consequences of treatment related to bone loss and jaw surgery. The speaker describes these combined physical issues as having "bamboozled" the client.

### Verbal and Physical Abuse
Used in the transcript to characterize the mother's behavior toward the father within the parental marriage. The client describes his mother as very verbally abusive of his father and at times physically threatening, citing one episode in which she picked up a sharp knife and threatened to kill him. Alcohol is noted as a contributing factor to the level of tension and reactivity between the parents.

### Foster Care / Adoption Agency Work
Referenced as a role the client's mother took on, described as taking care of foster children through work for an adoption agency in New York. This is noted as part of her transition from homemaker to employment outside the home before she later went to work for Verizon in 1970.
